subproblem.title: The divergence of a C¹ compactly supported vector field on ℝ^P is integrable with integral 0 (parent step 6)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P (Euclid P) be C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1) with compact support. Write div φ(z) := trace(Dφ(z)), the LinearMap.trace of fderiv ℝ φ z. Then div φ is Lebesgue integrable on ℝ^P and ∫_{ℝ^P} div φ dL^P = 0 (L^P = volume).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (φ : Euclid P → Euclid P), ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → HasCompactSupport φ → Integrable (fun z => LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid P) (fderiv ℝ φ z : Euclid P →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P)) ∧ ∫ z, LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid P) (fderiv ℝ φ z : Euclid P →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof step 6: for every C¹ compactly supported φ, ∫ div φ dL = 0, because each ∫ ∂_i φ^i dL vanishes by Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus.

Notation. e_1, …, e_P is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P (EuclideanSpace.single i 1, i.e. EuclideanSpace.basisFun). φ^i := ⟨e_i, φ⟩, K := tsupport φ (compact), L := L^P (volume), and ∂_i f(z) := Df(z)e_i.

1. Coordinates. Each φ^i = ⟨e_i, ·⟩ ∘ φ is C¹, being a composition with a continuous linear functional, and Dφ^i(z)w = ⟨e_i, Dφ(z)w⟩. φ^i vanishes outside K, so it has compact support. If P = 0, all sums below are empty and both claims are trivial.

2. Trace in coordinates. For every linear T : ℝ^P → ℝ^P, trace T = Σ_i ⟨e_i, T e_i⟩ (trace in an orthonormal basis). Hence div φ(z) = Σ_i ⟨e_i, Dφ(z)e_i⟩ = Σ_i ∂_iφ^i(z).

3. Integrability. Since φ^i is C¹, z ↦ ∂_iφ^i(z) is continuous. It vanishes outside K: φ^i vanishes on the open complement of the closed set tsupport φ^i, so its derivative is 0 there, and tsupport φ^i ⊆ K. So ∂_iφ^i is continuous with compact support, hence Lebesgue integrable. The finite sum div φ is therefore integrable too. This is the first conclusion.

4. ∫ ∂_iφ^i dL = 0 for each i. Write f := φ^i and choose R > 0 with K ⊆ B_R(0). Split z = (s, ẑ), where s = z_i ∈ ℝ and ẑ ∈ ℝ^{P−1} collects the other coordinates. This coordinate permutation is a measure-preserving linear isomorphism ℝ^P ≅ ℝ × ℝ^{P−1}, because Lebesgue measure is the product measure. Since ∂_if is integrable, Fubini gives ∫ ∂_if dL = ∫_{ℝ^{P−1}} (∫_ℝ ∂_if(s, ẑ) ds) dẑ. For fixed ẑ, u(s) := f(s, ẑ) is C¹ with u′(s) = ∂_if(s, ẑ), and u(s) = 0 for |s| ≥ R. By the fundamental theorem of calculus, ∫_ℝ u′ ds = ∫_{−R}^{R} u′ ds = u(R) − u(−R) = 0. Hence ∫ ∂_if dL = 0.
The Lean appendix uses an equivalent route. Since f is C¹ with compact support, it is Lipschitz. Mathlib's integration by parts for Lipschitz functions, LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq, applied to the constant function 1 (which is 0-Lipschitz) and to f in the direction e_i, gives ∫ (∂_{e_i}1)·f dL = ∫ 1·∂_{−e_i}f dL, i.e. 0 = −∫ ∂_if dL. The lemma integral_mul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_mul_of_integrable is not available under the contract imports.

5. Conclusion. By steps 2–4 and linearity of the integral (each summand is integrable), ∫ div φ dL = Σ_i ∫ ∂_iφ^i dL = 0. ∎

subproblem.title: Quantitative form of Simon 4.3 (1): normal averages converging to a unit vector give ∫_{B̄_r}⟨ν,v⟩dμ ≥ ½μ(B̄_r) for small r (parent step 1)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let μ be a measure on ℝ^P (Euclid P, Borel σ-algebra). Let ν : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be measurable with |ν(z)| ≤ 1 for all z, let y, v ∈ ℝ^P with |v| = 1, and let ρ₀ > 0 with μ(B̄_{ρ₀}(y)) < ∞. Suppose A(ρ) := μ(B̄_ρ(y))_ℝ^{−1} ∫_{B̄_ρ(y)} ν dμ → v as ρ ↓ 0, as a limit along 𝓝[>]0, with μ(·)_ℝ = ENNReal.toReal and 0^{−1} = 0. Then there is ρ₂ with 0 < ρ₂ ≤ ρ₀ such that ½ μ(B̄_r(y))_ℝ ≤ ∫_{B̄_r(y)} ⟨ν(z), v⟩ dμ(z) for every r with 0 < r < ρ₂.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ν : Euclid P → Euclid P) (y v : Euclid P) (ρ₀ : ℝ), 0 < ρ₀ → μ (closedBall y ρ₀) ≠ ∞ → Measurable ν → (∀ z, ‖ν z‖ ≤ 1) → ‖v‖ = 1 → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => (μ (closedBall y ρ)).toReal⁻¹ • ∫ z in closedBall y ρ, ν z ∂μ) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 v) → ∃ ρ₂ : ℝ, 0 < ρ₂ ∧ ρ₂ ≤ ρ₀ ∧ ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r < ρ₂ → (1 / 2 : ℝ) * (μ (closedBall y r)).toReal ≤ ∫ z in closedBall y r, inner ℝ (ν z) v ∂μ

1. Since w ↦ ⟨w, v⟩ is continuous, ⟨A(r), v⟩ → ⟨v, v⟩ = |v|² = 1 as r ↓ 0. As 1 > 1/2, there is ε > 0 with ⟨A(r), v⟩ > 1/2 for all r ∈ (0, ε); this is the definition of the limit along 𝓝[>]0.

2. Put ρ₂ := min(ε, ρ₀); then 0 < ρ₂ ≤ ρ₀. Fix r with 0 < r < ρ₂. Then r < ε and B̄_r ⊆ B̄_{ρ₀}, so μ(B̄_r) ≤ μ(B̄_{ρ₀}) < ∞.

4. If μ(B̄_r) = 0, both sides of the claim vanish: ½·0 = 0 = ∫_{B̄_r} ⟨ν, v⟩ dμ.

subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, y ∈ ℝ^P (Euclid P) and ρ, δ ∈ ℝ with ρ > 0 and δ > 0. Then there is ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ such that: (a) ζ is C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1); (b) ζ has compact support; (c) 0 ≤ ζ(z) ≤ 1 for all z; (d) ζ(z) = 1 for every z in the closed ball B̄_ρ(y); (e) tsupport ζ ⊆ B̄_{ρ+δ}(y); (f) the operator norm of Dζ(z) = fderiv ℝ ζ z satisfies ‖Dζ(z)‖ ≤ 3/(2δ) for every z; (g) Dζ(z) = 0 for every z ∉ B_{ρ+δ}(y) ∖ B̄_ρ(y) (B the open ball); (h) for every t with 0 < t ≤ 1 there is r ∈ ℝ with ρ ≤ r < ρ + δ and {z : t ≤ ζ(z)} = B̄_r(y).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof step 2: the C¹ cut-off that replaces Simon's Lipschitz cut-offs in Ch. 3, 4.3 (3)–(4), chapter-03.txt lines 621–636. The superlevel sets {ζ ≥ t} are described as in parent step 4. Three details below are filled in to justify the parent's assertions: the one-sided derivatives of the profile at 0 and 1, the Lipschitz bound for Dζ, and Fermat's theorem for the vanishing of Dζ.

Notation. |·| is the Euclidean norm on ℝ^P, B_r := B_r(y) is the open ball, B̄_r := B̄_r(y) is the closed ball, and Dζ(z) := fderiv ℝ ζ z has operator norm ‖Dζ(z)‖.

1. Profile. Let p(s) := 1 − 3s² + 2s³ = (1 − s)²(1 + 2s), c(s) := max(0, min(s, 1)), h(s) := p(c(s)) and q(s) := p′(c(s)) = −6c(s) + 6c(s)². Then c(s) = 0 for s ≤ 0, c(s) = s for 0 ≤ s ≤ 1, c(s) = 1 for s ≥ 1, and 0 ≤ c ≤ 1. Since p(0) = 1 and p(1) = 0, h = 1 on (−∞, 0], h = p on [0, 1] and h = 0 on [1, ∞). Also p′(s) = −6s + 6s², so p′(0) = p′(1) = 0.

2. h′ = q everywhere.
(a) If s < 0, h ≡ 1 on the neighbourhood (−∞, 0) of s, so h′(s) = 0 = q(s).
(b) If 0 < s < 1, h = p on the neighbourhood (0, 1), so h′(s) = p′(s) = q(s).
(c) If s > 1, h ≡ 0 on (1, ∞), so h′(s) = 0 = q(s).
(d) At s = 0: h ≡ 1 on (−∞, 0], so h has derivative 0 within (−∞, 0] at 0. Also h = p on [0, 1), a neighbourhood of 0 within [0, ∞), so h has derivative p′(0) = 0 within [0, ∞) at 0. The two one-sided derivatives coincide and (−∞, 0] ∪ [0, ∞) = ℝ, so h′(0) = 0 = q(0).
(e) At s = 1, symmetrically: h = p on (0, 1] gives derivative p′(1) = 0 within (−∞, 1], and h ≡ 0 on [1, ∞) gives derivative 0 within [1, ∞). So h′(1) = 0 = q(1).

3. Properties of h. q = p′ ∘ c is continuous, so h is differentiable with a continuous derivative, i.e. h ∈ C¹(ℝ). Since 0 ≤ c ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ c(1 − c) ≤ 1/4, q = −6c(1 − c) satisfies −3/2 ≤ q ≤ 0. Hence h is nonincreasing (h′ ≤ 0) and, by the mean value theorem, (3/2)-Lipschitz. Further 0 ≤ h ≤ 1, because h = (1 − c)²(1 + 2c) ≥ 0 and 1 − h = c²(3 − 2c) ≥ 0. Finally h(s) = 1 for s ≤ 0 and h(s) = 0 for s ≥ 1.

4. Definition of ζ and its support. Put a(z) := (|z − y| − ρ)/δ and ζ := h ∘ a. By step 3, 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1. If z ∈ B̄_ρ then a(z) ≤ 0, so ζ(z) = 1. If |z − y| ≥ ρ + δ then a(z) ≥ 1, so ζ(z) = 0. Hence support ζ ⊆ B_{ρ+δ} ⊆ B̄_{ρ+δ}. Since B̄_{ρ+δ} is closed, tsupport ζ = closure(support ζ) ⊆ B̄_{ρ+δ}. Since B̄_{ρ+δ} is compact and ζ vanishes outside it, ζ has compact support.

5. ζ is C¹. It suffices to show that ζ is C¹ at every z. If |z − y| < ρ, the open ball B_ρ is a neighbourhood of z on which ζ ≡ 1 (step 4), so ζ agrees with a constant near z and is C¹ at z. Otherwise |z − y| ≥ ρ > 0, so z − y ≠ 0. The Euclidean norm is C^∞ away from 0, so z′ ↦ |z′ − y| and a are C¹ at z, and ζ = h ∘ a is C¹ at z by the chain rule (h ∈ C¹ by step 3).

6. Gradient bound. For all z, w: |a(z) − a(w)| = ||z − y| − |w − y||/δ ≤ |z − w|/δ, so a is (1/δ)-Lipschitz. With step 3, ζ = h ∘ a is (3/2)·(1/δ) = 3/(2δ)-Lipschitz. The derivative of a Lipschitz function has operator norm at most the Lipschitz constant: |Dζ(z)w| = lim_{s→0} |ζ(z + sw) − ζ(z)|/|s| ≤ (3/(2δ))|w|. So ‖Dζ(z)‖ ≤ 3/(2δ) for every z.

7. Dζ vanishes off the open annulus. Let z ∉ B_{ρ+δ} ∖ B̄_ρ, i.e. |z − y| ≥ ρ + δ or |z − y| ≤ ρ. In the first case ζ(z) = 0 and ζ ≥ 0 everywhere. In the second case ζ(z) = 1 and ζ ≤ 1 everywhere (steps 3–4). So z is a local minimum or maximum of the differentiable function ζ, and Dζ(z) = 0 by Fermat's theorem. (Equivalently: where |z − y| ∉ {ρ, ρ + δ}, ζ is locally constant; where |z − y| ∈ {ρ, ρ + δ}, the chain rule gives Dζ(z) = δ^{−1}h′(a(z))·D|· − y|(z) with h′(0) = h′(1) = 0.)

8. Superlevel sets. Fix t ∈ (0, 1]. The set M := {s ∈ [0, 1] : h(s) ≥ t} is compact, being a closed subset of [0, 1] since h is continuous. It contains 0 because h(0) = 1 ≥ t. Let s_t := sup M; then s_t ∈ M and s_t ≥ 0. Moreover s_t < 1, since s_t = 1 would give t ≤ h(1) = 0.
Claim: for every real u, t ≤ h(u) ⇔ u ≤ s_t.
- If u ≤ s_t then h(u) ≥ h(s_t) ≥ t, because h is nonincreasing.
- Conversely, let t ≤ h(u) and suppose u > s_t. If u ≤ 1 then u ∈ [0, 1] (as u > s_t ≥ 0), so u ∈ M and u ≤ sup M = s_t, a contradiction. If u > 1 then h(u) = 0 < t, also a contradiction.
Now put r := ρ + δ s_t, so ρ ≤ r < ρ + δ. For every z, since δ > 0: t ≤ ζ(z) ⇔ a(z) ≤ s_t ⇔ |z − y| ≤ ρ + δ s_t = r ⇔ z ∈ B̄_r. Hence {z : t ≤ ζ(z)} = B̄_r.

9. Conclusion. The function ζ has all the required properties:
- it is C¹ (step 5);
- it has compact support and tsupport ζ ⊆ B̄_{ρ+δ} (step 4);
- 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1 and ζ = 1 on B̄_ρ (step 4);
- ‖Dζ‖ ≤ 3/(2δ) (step 6);
- Dζ = 0 off B_{ρ+δ} ∖ B̄_ρ (step 7);
- its superlevel sets are the closed balls of step 8. ∎

Suppose that c·μ({x : t ≤ ζ(x)})_ℝ ≤ ∫_{{x : t ≤ ζ(x)}} g dμ for every t with 0 < t ≤ 1. Then c·μ(B)_ℝ ≤ ∫_X ζ g dμ. Here μ(·)_ℝ = ENNReal.toReal and the integrals are Bochner integrals.

1. Inclusions. For t > 0, L_t ⊆ S, because x ∉ S gives ζ(x) = 0 < t. For t ≤ 1, B ⊆ L_t, because ζ = 1 ≥ t on B. Hence for t ∈ I, μ(B) ≤ μ(L_t) ≤ μ(S) < ∞, so μ(B)_ℝ ≤ μ(L_t)_ℝ.

2. Reduction to μ_S. ζg vanishes outside S, so ∫ ζ g dμ = ∫_S ζ g dμ = ∫ ζ g dμ_S. For t ∈ I, L_t ⊆ S gives ∫ 1_{L_t} g dμ_S = ∫_{L_t ∩ S} g dμ = ∫_{L_t} g dμ.

3. Layer-cake identity. Put H(x, t) := g(x) if t ≤ ζ(x), and H(x, t) := 0 otherwise. Fix x. Since 0 ≤ ζ(x) ≤ 1, {t ∈ I : t ≤ ζ(x)} = (0, ζ(x)], whose Lebesgue measure is ζ(x). Hence ∫_I H(x, t) dλ(t) = ζ(x) g(x).

4. Fubini. H is measurable on X × ℝ: the set {(x, t) : t ≤ ζ(x)} is measurable because (x, t) ↦ t and (x, t) ↦ ζ(x) are measurable, and g is measurable. Also |H| ≤ 1. The product μ_S ⊗ λ⌞I is a finite measure (total mass μ(S)·1), so H is integrable for it. Both factors are finite, hence s-finite, so Fubini's theorem gives ∫_X (∫_I H(x, t) dλ(t)) dμ_S(x) = ∫_I (∫_X H(x, t) dμ_S(x)) dλ(t). It also gives that t ↦ ∫_X H(x, t) dμ_S(x) is λ⌞I-integrable.

6. Lower bound. For t ∈ I, the hypothesis, step 1 and c ≥ 0 give ∫_{L_t} g dμ ≥ c μ(L_t)_ℝ ≥ c μ(B)_ℝ. Both sides are λ⌞I-integrable: the left by step 4, and the right is a constant on a set of measure 1. subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and D, F ⊆ ℝ^P (Euclid P) with F measurable. Let μ be a measure on ℝ^P, ν : ℝ^P → ℝ^P measurable with |ν(z)| ≤ 1 for all z, and y, v ∈ ℝ^P with |v| ≤ 1. Let ρ₂ ∈ ℝ with B̄_{ρ₂}(y) ⊆ D and μ(B̄_{ρ₂}(y)) < ∞. Assume two hypotheses. (GG): ∫_F div φ dL^P = −∫⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ for every C¹ map φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ D, where div φ = trace Dφ and L^P = volume. (1′): ½ μ(B̄_r(y))_ℝ ≤ ∫_{B̄_r(y)} ⟨ν, v⟩ dμ for every r with 0 < r < ρ₂ (μ(·)_ℝ = ENNReal.toReal). Then for all ρ, δ > 0 with ρ + δ < ρ₂, δ·μ(B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ 3·L^P(F ∩ (B_{ρ+δ}(y) ∖ B̄_ρ(y))) in [0, ∞], i.e. ENNReal.ofReal δ * μ(B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal 3 * volume(F ∩ (B_{ρ+δ}(y) ∖ B̄_ρ(y))).

This child uses the siblings radial_cutoff (Submission.codim1_rdo_dg_ce_radial_cutoff) and signed_layer_cake (Submission.codim1_rdo_dg_ce_signed_layer_cake). The parent applies it to (F, ν, v) and to (ℝ^{m+1} ∖ F, −ν, −v).

Fix ρ, δ > 0 with ρ + δ < ρ₂. Write B̄_r := B̄_r(y), A := B_{ρ+δ}(y) ∖ B̄_ρ(y), L := L^P (volume) and μ(·)_ℝ := ENNReal.toReal.

1. Finiteness. B̄_ρ ⊆ B̄_{ρ+δ} ⊆ B̄_{ρ₂} ⊆ D, so μ(B̄_ρ) ≤ μ(B̄_{ρ+δ}) ≤ μ(B̄_{ρ₂}) < ∞. A ⊆ B_{ρ+δ}(y) is a bounded Borel set, so L(F ∩ A) ≤ L(A) < ∞.

2. Cut-off (parent step 2). radial_cutoff with P, y, ρ, δ gives ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ with these properties:
- ζ is C¹ with compact support, 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1, and ζ = 1 on B̄_ρ;
- tsupport ζ ⊆ B̄_{ρ+δ};
- ‖Dζ(z)‖ ≤ 3/(2δ) for all z, and Dζ(z) = 0 for z ∉ A;
- for each t ∈ (0, 1], {ζ ≥ t} = B̄_r for some r with ρ ≤ r < ρ + δ.

3. Gauss–Green (parent step 3). Let φ(z) := ζ(z)v. It is C¹ (a C¹ scalar times a constant vector) and has compact support, with tsupport φ ⊆ tsupport ζ ⊆ B̄_{ρ+δ} ⊆ D. Its derivative is the rank-one map Dφ(z)w = (Dζ(z)w)v, whose trace is Dζ(z)v. Also ⟨φ(z), ν(z)⟩ = ζ(z)⟨v, ν(z)⟩. So (GG) gives
(i) ∫ ζ(z)⟨v, ν(z)⟩ dμ(z) = −∫_F Dζ(z)v dL(z).

4. Upper bound. For all z, |Dζ(z)v| ≤ ‖Dζ(z)‖|v| ≤ 3/(2δ), and Dζ(z)v = 0 for z ∉ A. So |Dζ(z)v| ≤ (3/(2δ))1_A(z). This bound is L⌞F-integrable because L(A) < ∞. Hence −∫_F Dζ v dL ≤ |∫_F Dζ v dL| ≤ ∫_F (3/(2δ))1_A dL = (3/(2δ))L(F ∩ A)_ℝ.

5. Lower bound (parent step 4). Apply signed_layer_cake with X = ℝ^P, μ, ζ, g(z) := ⟨v, ν(z)⟩, S := B̄_{ρ+δ}, B := B̄_ρ and c := ½. Its hypotheses hold:
- ζ is measurable (it is continuous), and g is measurable (ν is measurable and the inner product is continuous);
- 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1, and |g(z)| ≤ |v||ν(z)| ≤ 1 by Cauchy–Schwarz;
- S is closed, hence measurable, and μ(S) < ∞ by step 1;
- ζ(z) = 0 for z ∉ S, since such z lie outside tsupport ζ;
- ζ = 1 on B, and c ≥ 0;
- for t ∈ (0, 1], {ζ ≥ t} = B̄_r with 0 < ρ ≤ r < ρ + δ < ρ₂, so (1′) and the symmetry of the real inner product give ½μ(B̄_r)_ℝ ≤ ∫_{B̄_r} ⟨ν, v⟩ dμ = ∫_{{ζ≥t}} g dμ.
The conclusion is ½ μ(B̄_ρ)_ℝ ≤ ∫ ζ⟨v, ν⟩ dμ.

6. Combination (parent step 5). By (i) and steps 4–5, ½ μ(B̄_ρ)_ℝ ≤ (3/(2δ))L(F ∩ A)_ℝ. Multiplying by 2δ > 0 gives δ μ(B̄_ρ)_ℝ ≤ 3 L(F ∩ A)_ℝ.

7. Passage to [0, ∞]. μ(B̄_ρ) and L(F ∩ A) are finite (step 1), so ofReal(δ)·μ(B̄_ρ) = ofReal(δ μ(B̄_ρ)_ℝ) ≤ ofReal(3 L(F ∩ A)_ℝ) = ofReal(3)·L(F ∩ A). ∎
